title: Product form of the conditional special-pair law from fiber factorization
statement:
Fix a positive integer $n$, a deterministic disjointness protocol $p$ on inputs of length $n$, and an achievable value $z$ of the variable $Z = (M, T, X_{<T}, Y_{>T})$. Write $F$ for the fiber of $Z$ above $z$, and for a subset $S$ of the sample space let $\mathrm{vol}(S)$ denote its real-valued volume. Suppose that for every pair of bits $(b_1, b_2) \in \mathrm{Bool} \times \mathrm{Bool}$,
\[
\mathrm{vol}(F)\cdot\mathrm{vol}\!\left(F \cap \{\text{special bit-pair} = (b_1, b_2)\}\right)
= \mathrm{vol}\!\left(F \cap \{\text{Alice's special bit} = b_1\}\right)\cdot\mathrm{vol}\!\left(F \cap \{\text{Bob's special bit} = b_2\}\right).
\]
Then the conditional law of the special bit-pair on the fiber $F$ equals the product of the conditional law of Alice's special bit and the conditional law of Bob's special bit.
hypotheses_covered: p is a deterministic disjointness protocol on inputs of length n
z is an achievable value of the Z variable
for every bit-pair (b1,b2), the cross-multiplied fiber-volume factorization identity holds
replaced: A cross-multiplied version of singleton factorization, phrased using the original hard distribution instead of conditional fiber probabilities.
